- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16), model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast modestly to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after sentiment spikes) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if recent sentiment > 0.23 and price rises > 3% from prior day.  
- Model often lags in recognizing mean reversion — if sentiment turns negative after a peak, forecast should start trending down 1–2 days before true reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate final 5–7 days — adjust last 5–7 forecast points upward if sentiment remains positive or neutral.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to overcorrect — apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast to avoid overbought bias.
